guide.what: Option-adjusted spreads of AA, BBB (lowest investment grade) and CCC (junk) corporate bonds over Treasuries.
read: Widening spreads mean the market prices more default risk and sells credit; equities tend to follow down. Tightening is the opposite.
Junk moves first: CCC is the most sensitive and its moves are large (about 300 to 700bp in 2014-15, 300 to 1,000bp in 2020).
A reinforcing loop: wider spreads raise the cost of debt, which hurts cash flow and borrowing.
watch: Good but not always reliable, because the Fed reacts to stress. Read with real rates, the curve and the VIX.
FRED shows only about three years of ICE spreads; the Moody's Baa minus 10-year panel gives the long history.
